decisions.note: For the app, advise users to look for 100% pure, unrefined, or cold-pressed options, as commercial avocado oil is frequently adulterated with cheap seed oils.
For the database, advise users to check the label for high-quality sea salt or pink salt rather than refined table salt with anti-caking agents.

For the mobile app, recommend organic, unrefined, cold-pressed (virgin) coconut oil for daily use. Refined coconut oil is acceptable for high-heat cooking where a neutral flavor is needed, but users should avoid any versions that are chemically hydrogenated, as they contain harmful trans fats.

Explicitly tell users to avoid bottles generically labeled as a "vegetable oil blend" that happen to include mustard seed, as those are heavily processed. Look specifically for cold-pressed, pure mustard seed oil.

For your mobile app, the olive oil profile requires a prominent, multi-layered consumer warning system. While Extra Virgin Olive Oil (EVOO) is a top-tier health food, the commercial market is heavily plagued by widespread food fraud, rancidity, and misleading labeling.Your database should warn users to look for specific red flags and green lights when shopping.🛑 Red Flags: What to AvoidMisleading Words: Avoid labels reading "Pure," "Light," or "Pomace". These are highly refined, chemically treated oils stripped of their polyphenols and antioxidants.Clear Bottles: Never buy olive oil in clear glass or plastic containers. Light and heat rapidly oxidize the oil, turning a health food into a rancid source of inflammation.Vague Origins: Avoid bottles that state "Product of the E.U." or list a long string of multiple countries. This indicates a cheap, industrial blend of leftover crops that lack traceability.Missing Dates: If a bottle only lists a "Best By" date, skip it. A "Best By" date is tied to when it was packaged, meaning the oil inside could already be years old.🟢 Green Lights: What to Look ForHarvest Date: Look for a specific "Harvest Date" within the last 12 to 18 months. Olive oil is a fresh fruit juice; its health-giving polyphenols degrade steadily over time.Dark Packaging: Only purchase oil in opaque tins, dark amber, or dark green glass to protect it from light degradation.Single Country Origin: Choose bottles that name a specific estate, region, or single country of origin (e.g., 100% Californian, 100% Greek).Third-Party Certification Seals: Look for official verification stamps on the label. Examples include:The California Olive Oil Council (COOC) seal.The North American Olive Oil Association (NAOOA) certified seal.European PDO/DOP (Protected Designation of Origin) stamps.

For the mobile app, recommend 100% grass-fed and finished mutton tallow. Sheep are naturally pasture-centric animals, and grass-fed tallow contains significantly higher levels of anti-inflammatory Omega-3 fatty acids and Conjugated Linoleic Acid (CLA) than grain-finished alternatives.
